summary.headline: GEE Q4 FY26 turnover rose to INR112 crore and FY26 to about INR370 crore, with EBITDA margin near 9% and a 25-30% revenue CAGR target to FY29.
summary.overview: Management described Q4 FY26 turnover of about INR112 crore (up from INR79 crore in Q1 FY26), taking FY26 to roughly INR370 crore versus INR334 crore in FY25. Q4 EBITDA was about INR33 crore at a 9% margin, and PAT about INR13 crore (3.5% margin). Management framed FY26 as a stabilisation year after the May 2025 promoter restructuring, and set targets of INR1,000 crore revenue by FY29-30, FY27 revenue above INR500 crore and EBITDA margin above 10%. Growth is tied to defence, power (nuclear, thermal, hydro), railways and exports, with flux-cored wire production slated to start in July 2026.

financial_highlights.change: up from INR79 crore in Q1 FY26 (sequential)
management says FY25 margins were stabilised and exceeded in the last couple of years

financial_highlights.value: under 10% of revenue; around INR350-plus crore of INR370 crore is domestic
financial_highlights.change: down from a higher share in earlier years

segments.name: Specialised/defence products
segments.commentary: Management says GEE holds 70-80% share in defence welding consumables (Griduct 100, GEEFLUX 521); specialised applications business was about INR25 crore per an analyst's figure, which management did not confirm. FY26 defence business was INR10-12 crore, planned to more than double in FY27.

segments.name: Flux-cored wires
segments.commentary: Import-driven business of INR25-30 crore a year; in-house production expected from July 2026 under new BIS rules, with management targeting more than INR50 crore revenue a year and adding lines over time. INR20-30 crore capex identified for flux-cored lines and ancillary machines.

segments.name: Distribution vs direct B2B
segments.commentary: Management gave conflicting splits: 70-80% via distributors and 15-20% to end customers in one answer, and about 25-30% direct B2B and 65-70% via distributors in another. Management said B2B share is rising from 20-25% toward 30-40%.

segments.name: Exports
segments.commentary: Export share is under 10% of revenue, down from earlier years. Approvals were obtained from ADNOC (UAE) and a Saudi breakthrough, with NAKS approval from Russia in trial. Management targets export growth more than three times within two years, using TUV approval for stainless TIG wire for Europe.

guidance_outlook: Revenue target: 25-30% CAGR till FY29, reaching INR1,000 crore around FY29-30; FY27 revenue above INR500 crore.
EBITDA: FY27 EBITDA margin above 10%; Keshav Garg's annualised INR45 crore EBITDA for FY27 was confirmed by management, with Q1 seasonally weaker.
Longer term, management targets 13%+ sustained EBITDA margin, and a further INR1,000 crore via acquisitions over 5-6 years (INR2,000 crore total).
Management expects finance cost to fall in FY27 from solar installation and better working capital, and expects working capital and cash flow to improve.
Thane land development agreement (13,000+ sq m at Wagle Industrial Estate) expected to generate more than INR400 crore cash over five years.
capex_capacity: Capacity utilisation about 57%, targeted to rise to 80-90% through ancillary lines (drawing machines to feed extrusion machines); some machines already ordered.
Flux-cored wire production to start July 2026; machine dispatch in May 2026; capacity to be added in lines over time.
Submerged arc flux line with 30-35 metric tonne per day capacity recently started.
Capex of INR20-30 crore identified for ancillary machines and flux-cored wire lines, including shifting machines from the Thane plot to another facility.
Solar power installation in factories planned for this year or next to lower power cost and finance cost; management says growth to INR1,000 crore needs little capex.
demand_pricing: Management cites defence, power (nuclear, thermal, hydro), railways (20,000+ bogie order expected), exports and shipbuilding as growth drivers; NPCIL approval received about two weeks before the call.
Inconel electrodes priced INR2,500-3,500 per kg, with a pending order above 20 tonnes; cobalt alloys INR3,500-5,500 per kg, with business above INR10 crore last year, targeted to double.
Pricing: management says GEE is 6-7% below ESAB and Ador in retail/distributor channels, but at par in project (tender) business.
Commodity inflation is passed to customers with about a one-month lag, per management.
Management says the Indian welding market is INR15,000-20,000 crore; GEE targets 10-15% share, and the organised share is 50-60% after GST.

qa_highlights.question: Which sectors will drive the 25-30% growth and what is the current sector-wise revenue split?
qa_highlights.answer: Management named power, railways, exports and defence as main drivers and declined to give a sector split, saying L&T and BHEL buy across all sectors.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Q4 EBITDA run-rate annualisable to about INR45 crore for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Payal Agarwal said yes, INR45 crore EBITDA is the target for FY27, with Q1 seasonally weaker due to monsoon and labour shortage.

qa_highlights.question: How many specialised-application volumes make up the roughly 36,000 tonnes volume and what is the realisation difference?
qa_highlights.answer: Management did not give the figure and said it would revert with the exact numbers.

qa_highlights.question: What is the R&D expense for the last two years?
qa_highlights.answer: Management did not give a number; it said R&D costs are moderate, with heavy lab equipment (e.g. an XRF machine from Germany) capitalised rather than expensed.

qa_highlights.question: How does the 3x revenue growth square with 48-58% utilisation?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said growth will come from ancillary lines to lift utilisation to 80-90%, new products such as flux-cored wires, and higher-value specialised products.

qa_highlights.question: What are the proceeds of the Thane land used for and will there be a distribution?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said a dividend is under consideration and proceeds would fund acquisitions of welding equipment and safety/maintenance product companies; one or two deals are targeted within a year.

risks_watch: Revenue targets are long-dated (FY29-30) and rely on new approvals (NPCIL, Adani Power, TUV, ADNOC, Russia) that are still in trial or testing.
Management gave inconsistent B2B vs distributor splits and did not provide R&D expense, specialised-product volume, or sector breakdown when asked.
Flux-cored wire start-up is set for July 2026; any delay would push the INR50 crore revenue target.
Pricing gap vs ESAB and Ador in retail (6-7% lower), with competitive pressure in tender business.
Employee cost to rise in FY27 with sales hiring; margin delivery depends on commodity pass-through and cost control.
Acquisition-led growth to INR2,000 crore is not yet supported by any identified deal.
summary.management_tone: Confident and expansive on growth, defence and the long-term INR1,000 crore vision, but vague and inconsistent on operating detail: sector split, B2B mix, R&D spend and specialised volumes were deferred or not quantified.
key_quotes: So, the target revenue is to grow and take this company in the short term to a INR 1,000 crore company.
We are looking at a 25% to 30% target revenue growth CAGR till FY29.
We are looking at a double digit plus actually. We are looking at a 10% plus margin EBITDA margin and we are looking at a INR 500 crore plus top line as well.
So, INR45 crores of EBITDA, of course, is something that we are looking at for this year as well.

growth.why: Guided 25-30% revenue CAGR to FY29 and FY27 revenue above INR500 crore (about 35% on FY26 INR370 crore, roughly 50% per the brief's implied base), with FY27 EBITDA margin above 10%; backing is partly specific (flux-cored lines from July 2026, INR20-30 crore capex, ancillary drawing machines, 57% utilisation rising to 80-90%) but export and 1,000 crore goals lack contracts or timelines.
